details.label: Discussion
details.text: A cumulus field with convective showers, just south of Lake Erie, continues to grow within the warm sector, just south of a broad precipitation band that is contributing to local baroclinicity. On the warm side of the baroclinic boundary, insolation is supporting surface temperatures climbing into the 80s F, amid 70s F dewpoints, yielding MLCAPE up to 1000 J/kg in negligible MLCINH. The current thinking is that storms should continue to expand in coverage while gradually intensifying. A 500 mb jet streak is currently overspreading the Midwest and is poised to reach the northern Appalachians in approximately 4-6 hours. As this occurs, vertical wind shear will also increase, with 40-50 kts of effective bulk shear expected. When this occurs, multicells, transient supercells, and short line segments will all become possible, accompanied by mainly a damaging gust threat. Additionally, storms anchored along the baroclinic boundary may also produce a brief tornado. Given current shear limitations, it is unclear if or when a more widespread severe threat will materialize. Therefore, convective trends will continue to be monitored for the need of a Severe Thunderstorm Watch issuance
